annotations.text:
Current home, pixel-matched to app/actions/home.tsx + public/styles/app.css.
Real seed data: 3 ongoing / 2 in process / 2 completed / 1 cancelled, feed ordered id DESC.

What it costs: the 2x2 status grid eats 162px, so only ~5 of 8 tasks are visible before scrolling — and the first two are Cancelled and Completed, which are the two you can do nothing about.

A · Denser feed — axis: how much of the backlog fits on one screen.
Status grid collapses to a 48px chip row; task cards drop the 45.6px ring for a 4px bar. All 8 tasks fit with no scroll.

Tradeoff: the status counts lose their poster-sized presence, and the progress ring — the most distinctive thing in the current design — is gone.

B · Hero task — axis: does the home screen answer "what do I do now?"
One large card for the next due task with status pill, step count, assignee stack and an Open action; counts shrink to a dot legend; everything else becomes a one-line row.

Tradeoff: needs a rule for picking the hero (soonest due? most progress?), and that rule will be wrong sometimes. Wasteful if you mostly browse rather than execute.

C · Week strip — axis: time instead of recency.
Week of 24-30 Aug with per-day load dots, status tabs reusing the existing .tabs pattern, feed sorted by due date with today's card outlined coral. All 8 seed tasks land in one week, so the strip is genuinely informative.

Tradeoff: most vertical chrome of the three (62px strip + 33px tabs), and it breaks down for tasks with no due date — the schema allows dueDate: null.
